seo.whatIsDesc: A modern, learn-while-playing Minesweeper. Classic 9×9 / 16×16 / 16×30 boards and flagging, plus a Learn Mode that computes the mine probability for every unopened cell in real time, overlays a 75% green-yellow-red heatmap, and scores each move 0-10 against the optimal choice. No right-click required — double-click to chord, perfect for trackpads and phones.
howToPlay: Left-click to open. First click never hits a mine; numbers show mines in the 8 neighbors.
Right-click / long-press to flag. The header shows mines remaining.

Double-click to chord (Apple / trackpad optimized): classic chording needs left+right together. Here, if flags around a number equal the number, double-click the number to open the rest — no right-click needed. Desktop left+right still works, and chording counts as a perfect 10.
Open all non-mine cells to win; hit a mine and the board reveals.
seo.heatmapDesc: With Learn Mode on, a solver builds constraints need = number - flags from opened numbers, splits frontier cells into components and enumerates, while isolated cells share the remaining mines evenly. Each cell gets P(mine) 0-1, shown as green (0%) → yellow (50%) → red (100%) at 75% opacity. Toggle % and fraction independently — color alone trains intuition.
seo.efficiencyTitle: Decision efficiency: how good was that move?
seo.efficiencyDesc: No absolute 10 — only relative to the board. Open: score=(1-p)/(1-pMin)*10 where pMin is the current safest cell; Flag: score=p/pMax*10. Picking the safest/riskiest at that moment is 10; picking 50% when 0% exists is ~5. Chording is always 10. Scores share the solver, so closing the heatmap still records for the post-game chart.
seo.chartTitle: How to read the replay chart
seo.chartDesc: It pops up at game over. X is time, left Y is speed, right Y is quality — 4 lines, two rhythms:
chartBullets: Open safe (teal · left): RPM background, bucketed every 6s — raw speed & flood-fill bursts.
Flag (red · left): RPM background, also 6s buckets — when you were flagging.

Efficiency (orange dots+line · right 0-10): plotted at the exact click time. 10 = optimal at that moment; <5 red, 5-9 orange, 10 green. Click any dot to highlight that cell on the board and trace the low score.
Mine prob (purple triangles, dashed · right 0-10 = prob×10): only for open/chord, the P(mine) of that cell at that moment. Overlay it with orange — high purple + low orange = a risky guess.
seo.chartHint: How to use it: find valleys in orange, check if purple spikes at the same time — that's the move to review. Click the dot, the board highlights the cell; next time pick a greener one.
progressSteps: Start with heatmap on, learn green=open, red=flag intuition;
Turn off %/fraction, decide by color alone, still aim for 10;
Turn Learn Mode off and challenge Hard 16×30 — keep RPM steady and orange ≥9.

items.a: Meathill Minesweeper (minesweeper.meathill.com) is a learn-while-playing Minesweeper with 9×9/16×16/16×30 boards, no right-click required, double-click chording, and Learn Mode: live probability heatmap + efficiency scoring with post-game replay.

Constraints need = number - flags on frontier cells, split into components and enumerated exactly, isolated cells share remaining mines evenly, yielding P(mine) 0-1 as green→yellow→red 75% overlay. Solver always runs for scoring.

Relative, not absolute. Open: (1-p)/(1-pMin)*10, flag: p/pMax*10, chord always 10. Picking the safest/most certain cell at that moment is 10; picking 50% when 0% exists is ~5. Each orange dot in the replay is one score — click it to highlight the cell.

items.q: How to chord on Apple / trackpad?
items.a: Optimized: no left+right needed — double-click any opened number where flags == number to open the rest. Right-click, long-press, and trackpad all work, plus mobile.

items.q: How to read the replay chart?
items.a: Left Y = speed, right Y = quality. X is time, two RPM lines (teal=open, red=flag, left) are 6s-bucketed background; two scatter lines (orange=efficiency 0-10, purple=mine prob×10, right) are plotted at the exact click time. Sustained 9+ in orange means optimal; click a valley — if purple spikes there, it was a high-risk guess on that highlighted cell.

Beginners use heatmap for intuition, intermediates use color only, experts turn Learn Mode off for Hard. Every game is reviewable.
Site: https://minesweeper.meathill.com/ · Studio: Meathill Studio
